title: Get deep into the problem. Find what matters.
navTitle: Get deep into the problem. Find what matters.
description: DDA investigates hard public, industrial, and institutional problems in British Columbia and across Canada. We find the constraint that shapes the outcome.

title: What we do
description: DDA finds what controls an outcome and what must change for it to change. Six kinds of analysis and thirteen areas of work in BC and across Canada.
metaTitle: What we do | Six kinds of analysis

title: Evidence reconstruction
description: DDA traces every figure to its primary source, records its status, and shows where sources disagree. The result is an evidence base a hostile reader can check.
metaTitle: Evidence reconstruction and source tracing | DDA

title: Economic and market analysis
description: Economic impact and market analysis for BC public and industrial decisions. DDA measures what an action adds, what it moves, and what leaves the region.
metaTitle: Economic impact and market analysis in BC | DDA

title: Fiscal and scenario modelling
description: Fiscal impact analysis and scenario modelling for BC municipalities and public bodies. DDA tests which assumption carries the result.
metaTitle: Fiscal impact analysis and modelling in BC | DDA

title: Labour and workforce analysis
description: Labour market analysis for BC projects and communities, including labour market research plans. DDA finds the usable supply below the workforce total.
metaTitle: Labour market analysis in BC | DDA

title: Land, infrastructure, and spatial analysis

metaTitle: Employment lands and land capacity analysis | DDA

title: Institutional and policy analysis

title: Housing and municipal planning

title: When a housing target is larger than delivery
navTitle: When a housing target is larger than delivery
description: A housing target can be fully defensible and still tell a council little about delivery. A small-community case traces need through the delivery chain.
finding: At an even rate, that is about 14.5 units a year. From 2009 to 2019, the Village built 36 units, or 3.6 a year, according to its 2024 land disposition RFP.
metaTitle: Housing targets and delivery rates | DDA

title: The trade gap hidden inside a workforce number
navTitle: The trade gap hidden inside a workforce number
description: A project can have enough workers on paper and still miss its date. An Eskay Creek analysis finds the gap in one trade, one phase, one window.
finding: In this analysis the commissioning phase needs about 90 pipefitters. The analysis found about 30 available in the region. The gap is 60 people, or 67 percent of the requirement.
metaTitle: The trade gap in a workforce number: Eskay Creek | DDA

title: When an unsupported number carries the answer
navTitle: When an unsupported number carries the answer
description: Some inputs carry a whole decision. DDA finds them, checks their source, and shows what changes if they move.
finding: The conclusion, that labour is available, depends on four conditions that the evidence does not establish.
metaTitle: When an unsupported number carries the answer | DDA
